channel.description: Founding Researcher, PAVO AI · Research Fellow, Secrier Lab, UCL

item.title: Can We Imitate the Steps by Which Humans Understand the World?
item.description: A formal model for an agent that reads papers, runs small experiments and evaluates candidates. It records current hypotheses and uncertainty, chooses actions by expected information gain per cost, and updates only from verified evidence. The model also separates belief updates, graph adoption and expansion of the hypothesis space.

item.title: 我和openclaw
item.description: 我在 Mac mini 上搭了一套全天在线的个人 agent 系统。起初只是试着装软件，后来有一段时间，我每天只和它对话：邮件、新闻、生活记录，都由它替我处理。最后，我却因为维护太费心而离开了 OpenClaw。这篇文章按五个阶段回顾这段经历，整理出十九项需求，也看看已有的开源项目能帮到哪一步。

item.title: Measuring Agent Safety with Control Barrier Functions
item.description: A framework for measuring safety margins along an LLM agent trajectory. It defines an abstract state, a barrier function and a filter, then compares three ways to construct them: from tool schemas, from an environment model, or by learning. Each is discussed alongside related work in autonomous driving, with its assumptions and limits made explicit.

item.title: Lifelong Learning, Formally: Objects, Boundaries, Schools
item.description: A three-layer formalisation of lifelong learning: the mathematical objects (a hidden generator with a variation budget, regimes, an agent of bounded size, what its policy really holds, a bounded-capacity oracle, dynamic regret), three criteria that separate lifelong learning from eight neighbouring paradigms, and twelve schools of existing method sorted by the three challenges they answer. With the lineage of every piece, and a note on why survival, not regret, is the real score.

item.title: A Company in a Box: physics, a server sandbox, and a two-tier agent team
item.description: A sandbox for studying how LLM agents run a small ride-hailing business. It combines a street simulation, a working deployment pipeline, a shared operating budget and three roles with separate permissions. Includes four views of one run and observations about how the team makes decisions.

item.title: Cognitive Operators: Measuring Where Model Performance Breaks Down
item.description: Results from 27 cognitive probes across nine models in three families. A look at accuracy over difficulty, lookup shortcuts, probe redesign and how the findings might inform agent harnesses.

item.title: How Task Partitioning and Communication Limit Multi-Agent Collaboration
item.description: An introduction to our information-theoretic study of multi-agent systems: the information lost when a task is split, why internal communication cannot recover it, and what external feedback changes.

item.title: How far are we from automating the whole training run?
item.description: Two pipelines taken apart into the steps a person once did by hand, and every method since 2018 placed on the cell it automated. By 2026 what is left for people is judgement, not labour. Interactive: click any cell for the method in symbols and for grandma; pick the axes (time, pipeline stage, compute cost, human cost) to re-plot the field.

item.title: Simulating Human Behaviour with LLMs: A Literature Map
item.description: A map of 132 papers on LLM survey participants, organised by problems, methods and evaluation, with a discussion of SEM for testing psychometric structure.
